analysis.title: Nasdaq at the breaking point, what happens next could be violent
key_insights: NDX futures printed a large hammer candle yesterday at the trend line that has held since the April lows, converging with the 100-day moving average. The Market Ear calls this a must-hold zone for tech.

Semiconductor volumes spiked in the washout. SMH and DRAM both recorded their highest trading volumes in quite some time, and some of it may reflect forced selling from de-grossing rather than a change in conviction.
Tech CDS spreads are rising alongside falling tech stocks this time. The earlier CDS spike coincided with a surging NDX, so credit and equities now agree.
VXN is approaching its September highs, but tech volatility has been range-bound for two months.

Goldman's Privorotsky says global systematic long/short funds fell 1.4% yesterday, a nearly four-standard-deviation move. The stress is in gross exposure, with short squeezes alongside heavy selling of longs.
Privorotsky expects more choppiness but is increasingly optimistic that semis are at levels where much of the bad news is priced in. One relative-value idea is short hyperscalers versus semis.
Privorotsky sees stabilization in the most leveraged parts of the AI complex after a sharp reversal off yesterday's lows and suspects a local bottom, as credit fears were overdone in the short term.

The structural problem Privorotsky flags is too much capital chasing too little power-ready compute capacity. The repricing could be gradual or come through violent dislocations that spill into broader markets.
Spot compute rental pricing remains strong for B200s, H200s, H100s and A100s despite rapid depreciation, which favors owners of existing infrastructure.

NDX and the US 10-year yield have moved together since September. The Market Ear reads this as growth and risk appetite dominating the discount-rate narrative, so lower yields are not bullish for tech if they fall on growth worries.
NDX forward P/E is back near 21x, the low of the AI cycle since 2023. Peter Callahan says this could support the run into earnings season, with earnings doing more of the lifting.

sector_views.rationale: Privorotsky is increasingly optimistic that semis have reached levels where much of the bad news is priced in. Short hyperscalers versus semis is a possible relative-value trade.

earnings_insights: Peter Callahan says NDX forward P/E near 21x could support the run into earnings season, with earnings potentially doing much of the lifting. No company-level figures are given.

macro_indicators.interpretation: NDX and the 10-year yield have moved in tandem since September. Lower yields are not necessarily bullish for tech if they fall because of growth concerns.
Privorotsky calls high oil prices a headwind alongside the relief from lower yields.

trade_ideas.description: Relative value: short hyperscalers versus long semiconductors
trade_ideas.rationale: Privorotsky sees semis at levels where much of the bad news is priced in, while hyperscalers face AI financing and capex pressure.

risk_factors: A break of the NDX trend line from the April lows and the 100-day moving average could turn the move ugly quickly.
Tech credit stress and rising CDS spreads.
Financing and power constraints on AI capex are not going away.
Violent repricing of AI capital and compute capacity could spill into broader markets.
vol_and_positioning: VXN is approaching its September highs while tech vol has been range-bound for two months.
Global systematic long/short funds fell 1.4% in one day, about a four-standard-deviation move, driven by gross de-grossing rather than net exposure.
Violent short squeezes alongside aggressive selling of longs point to widespread de-grossing.
SMH and DRAM saw their highest trading volumes in quite some time, possibly forced selling.
Positioning is described as increasingly washed out.

tension_points.bull_case: A hold at the April trend line and 100-day moving average, with a hammer candle, washed-out positioning and 21x forward P/E, could set up a powerful squeeze.
tension_points.bear_case: A break of those levels, with credit stress building and long/short books de-grossing, could get ugly fast.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break of the trend line that has held since the April lows and the 100-day moving average.
